source.attribution: SAMPLE DATA: synthetic prices generated by Mycelium Backtest from a fixed seed. Not real market data.

gaps.note: Missing bars are compared with the NYSE calendar; no bar is invented.

assumptions: Spot instruments: no leverage, no margin, long and short treated symmetrically.
No funding, borrow, financing or dividend costs are modelled.
Signals are evaluated at the close of a bar; entries and signal exits fill at the open of the next bar.
Slippage is adverse on every fill, entry and exit: 2 basis points.
Fees on every fill: 0.05% of notional plus 0 fixed.
Position size: 100% of equity per trade, no leverage, computed on the initial capital.
Stops and targets are checked from the entry bar, using each bar's high and low.
When one bar reaches both the stop and the target, the stop is assumed hit first.
A bar that opens beyond the stop or the target fills at its open, not at the level.
Fill prices are not rounded to the tick size.
At most 1 trade(s) per session; one position at a time.
Positions exit at the close after 10 bar(s) held.

checks.headline: Profitable before costs, not after: costs take 177% of gross
checks.detail: Gross P&L before costs 55.20; fees 69.98 and slippage 27.99 leave a net of -42.77. Re-run with costs at 2x: net -136.65. Re-run with no costs: net 51.24.

checks.headline: Only 7 trades: too few to judge
checks.detail: 7 trades in total (100 or more passes, fewer than 30 fails). The chronological split gives 4 trades in the first 70% and 3 in the last 30%. At least 30 per part are needed, so the split results are flagged as insufficient.

checks.headline: Without the best trade the result is -103.16
checks.detail: The best trade made 60.39. Without it the net P&L is -103.16 and the profit factor 0.45 (n/a means no losing trade). Fewer than 30 trades: the sample is too small to judge.

checks.headline: Profitable early, then -93.41 in the last 30%
checks.detail: First 70% of trades (4): net 50.64, profit factor 1.58. Last 30% (3): net -93.41, profit factor 0.07. The split is by trade order, not by date, and the strategy rules are the same in both parts. Each part needs at least 30 trades; this split is insufficient to judge.

checks.headline: Beats only 66% of random-entry runs
checks.detail: 1,000 draws, each with 7 trades that keep the real holding durations but enter at random bars, long only, with the same costs and position size. The real net P&L -42.77 beats 66.1% of the draws (median -88.86, 5th to 95th percentile -275.06 to 76.61). This measures how often random timing did as well on this data; it does not show that the strategy will keep working, and a high percentile can still be luck. Fewer than 30 trades: too few to judge.

checks.headline: No overall profit to spread across periods
checks.detail: Trades cut into 1 equal blocks by trade count, in time order; net P&L per block: -42.77. Positive blocks: 0%. The total is not positive, so there is no profit to spread. Too few trades for a reliable period comparison. Parameter sweep: 25 of 25 settings of oversold and exit_rsi run; 8 of 8 neighbours of the chosen setting evaluated, 38% of them profitable. Best setting in the grid: 110.42 (an isolated spike).

verdict.label: Not credible
verdict.sentence: Not credible if the costs, random-entry or trade-count check fails, or if two or more checks fail. Credible only if no check fails, at most one warns, the out-of-sample and random-entry checks pass and no check lacks data. Fragile otherwise.

calendar.rule: Each trade counts on the session date of its exit bar, in the market's session time zone (New York for US stocks; the configured anchor and time zone for crypto). Days without a session, and session days outside the data, are left empty, not zero.

assumptions: Past results do not predict future results. This report describes one backtest on one data set.
Costs are modelled from the fees and slippage you set; real fills can be worse.
The costs check re-runs the same rules with no costs and with costs at 2x.
The out-of-sample check splits trades in time order, 70/30; the rules were not re-fitted on the first part, so this is a consistency check, not a true walk-forward test.

Random entries: 1,000 draws with seed 1, the same number of trades and holding durations, random entry bars and directions, trades kept in their original order. Random trades have no stop or target, because those come from the signal logic being tested; they exit after the same number of bars as the real trade they mirror.
Random trades of one draw may overlap in time, unlike the real run, which holds one position at a time.
Random trades use the run's costs; with fixed-fraction sizing on the initial capital they use the same sizing rule, otherwise the notional of the real trade they mirror.
Period robustness cuts trades into up to 4 equal blocks by trade count, not by calendar time.
A check with fewer than 30 trades, or fewer than 30 per split, is flagged as lacking data and never passes.
The parameter sweep re-runs the full engine for each setting on the same data; a profitable neighbourhood is evidence of stability, not of future profit.

method.label: ESTIMATED FROM CANDLES
method.volume_rule: Each candle's volume is spread over its low-high range with a density of 2 inside the body (between open and close) and 1 on the wicks; each price row receives the share of that density that falls inside it. A candle with no range puts all its volume in the row of its price. The buy share of a candle is (close - low) / (high - low), 0.5 when the range is zero; it is an estimate, not observed order flow.
method.normalisation: intensity = min(1, log(1 + v / m) / log(1 + p / m)), where v is the cell volume, m the median and p the 99th percentile of the non-empty cells; empty cells are 0.
